key: (The Tao) produces (all things) and nourishes them; it produces them and does not claim them as its own; it does all, and yet does not boast of it; it presides over all, and yet does not control them. This is what is called ‘The mysterious Quality’ (of the Tao).
s: The chapter calls producing and nourishing without claiming, boasting or controlling ‘The mysterious Quality’; Wang Bi, on chapter 10, reads producing as not blocking the source of things and nourishing as not restraining their nature, so that things are born and grow of themselves, and takes the mystery as virtue that has no master.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 10, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

evidence.words: 不塞其原，則物自生，何功之有。不禁其性，則物自濟，何為之恃。物自長足，不吾宰成，有德無主，非玄而何。
evidence.gloss: If their source is not blocked, things are born of themselves: what merit is there? If their nature is not restrained, things complete themselves: what doing is there to rely on? Things grow and suffice of themselves, not ruled and completed by me: there is virtue and no master. What is that if not mysterious?

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 10, at [9]); Wang Bi's base text (生之，畜之。生而不有，為而不恃，長而不宰，是謂玄德) is the line of the key verse. His comments gloss 生之 as 不塞其原 and 畜之 as 不禁其性, and the comment on the closing line carries 物自生, 物自長足 and 有德無主，非玄而何; the sentence paraphrases these without drift. Plain sense restates the key verse and does not lean on Legge's parentheses; three quoted words. entry-check ok.
